anomalies.observed: The WS2812B status LED data input (D4, DIN) is wired to net NET0008, and the same net NET0008 is also the signal pin of the 4-pin +12 V/GND fan header J13 (pin 3) on the Power sheet. NET0008 additionally terminates only on the fan-tach protection cluster (D2/D10/R6/R7/D3/D7) on the MCU sheet and is not connected to any ESP32-C3 GPIO pin.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the board 'Monitors 2 fan tachometers (NUM_FANS = 2) with TVS-diode-protected inputs' and exposes 'a single onboard WS2812B status LED (D1)' driven by the MCU. The fan-tach line and the WS2812B data line must be two separate nets, each reaching its own ESP32 GPIO; the WS2812B DIN must be driven by a MCU output, not tied to a fan tachometer input.

evidence.quote: MCU sheet (sheet 1/4, /Microcontroller/): D4 WS2812B, DIN pin labelled NET0008
Power sheet (sheet 3/4, /Power/): J13 Conn_01x04_Pin, pin 3 labelled NET0008 (with pin 1 = +12 V, pin 4 = GND)
Monitors 2 fan tachometers (NUM_FANS = 2) with TVS-diode-protected inputs, and raises a run fault if a fan stalls.
a single onboard WS2812B status LED (D1)

anomalies.impact: The MCU's WS2812B data stream is shorted to a fan tachometer output (open-drain), so neither the status LED nor the fan-speed measurement can work; the WS2812B receives corrupted data and the fan stall detection is defeated. Because NET0008 also never reaches an ESP32 GPIO, both the LED and that fan input are effectively unconnected to the controller.

parsed.summary: Most of the design matches the specification (power mux, buck, heater high-side switch, three shared-bus MAX31855 thermocouples on GPIO5/10 with CS on GPIO4/6/7, USB-C CC pull-downs, correct passive values), but the WS2812B status-LED data net (NET0008) is merged with a fan tachometer header net and is not routed to any MCU GPIO, which is a cross-signal bridging anomaly.
